questions.question_text:
A quantity obeys $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=kQ$, with $Q(0)=250$ and $Q(5)=1000$.
Find the exact value of $k$.

options.why: Formed the ratio the wrong way round, dividing the initial value by the later value.
Multiplied by the time instead of dividing by it when solving $5k=\ln 4$.
Inverted the ratio and also multiplied by the time instead of dividing.

questions.question_text:
A radioactive sample satisfies $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=kA$, with $t$ in years.
Its initial mass is $200$ g, and after $3$ years its mass is $120$ g. Find its mass after $6$ years.

options.why: Subtracted the same loss of $80$ g in each $3$-year period instead of multiplying by the same proportion.
Used only one $3$-year decay period instead of two.
Used the lost proportion $0.4$ as the remaining proportion in each period, calculating $200(0.4)^2$.

questions.question_text:
A population satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=0.12P$, with $t$ in years.
How long does the population take to triple, correct to one decimal place?

options.why: Used $\ln 2$, which gives the doubling time rather than the tripling time.
Divided $3$ by $0.12$ without taking the logarithm first.
Used $\log_{10}3$ instead of $\ln 3$.

questions.question_text:
A sample of $800$ g decays to $700$ g in $4$ years, and satisfies $\dfrac{dm}{dt}=km$.
Find the mass after $10$ years, correct to the nearest gram.

options.why: Treated the loss as a constant $25$ g per year instead of a constant proportion.
Treated $10$ years as two complete $4$-year periods, using $800\left(\frac{7}{8}\right)^{2}$.
Treated $10$ years as three complete $4$-year periods, using $800\left(\frac{7}{8}\right)^{3}$.

questions.question_text:
A quantity $N$ satisfies $\dfrac{dN}{dt}=kN$, with $N(0)=7$ and $N(3)=189$.
Which equation gives $N$ as a function of $t$?

options.why: Inverted the ratio of the readings, giving a negative value of $k$.
Used $\ln 27$ for $k$ without dividing by the elapsed time of $3$.
Used the later reading $189$ as the initial amount instead of $7$.

questions.question_text:
A quantity satisfies $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=kQ$, with $t$ in years.
It takes $9$ years for $Q$ to fall to one third of its value.
Find how long it takes to fall to $5\%$ of its original value, correct to the nearest year.

options.why: Rounded $5\%$ to $\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{3}\approx 3.7\%$ and counted three complete $9$-year stages.
Treated the decay as linear, losing two thirds of the original amount every $9$ years.

questions.question_text:
A population is modelled by $P=3000e^{0.06t}$, with $t$ in years.
Find the population after $25$ years, correct to the nearest ten.

options.why: Grew the population by $6\%$ of the initial value each year, treating the growth as linear.
Used $3000(1.06)^{25}$, the annual compounding form, instead of $3000e^{0.06\times 25}$.
